extracted.intended_audience: novice-to-intermediate grant writers and nonprofit staff seeking foundation, state, federal, or corporate funding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for developing competitive grant proposals (executive summary through budget, evaluation, and sustainability) and related preparatory tasks such as prospect research and LOIs, aimed at organizations seeking external funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key distinction: Grants vs. Contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants: Funds awarded to support specific projects or activities. Contracts: Agreements for specific deliverables or services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the distinction to determine proposal style and obligations — grants emphasize project impact and fit with funder priorities; contracts emphasize defined deliverables and performance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding source categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal grants; State grants; Foundation grants (private and community foundations); Corporate grants (corporate giving programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target proposals and compliance to the appropriate funder type (e.g., federal systems like Grants.gov for federal grants). Understand differing expectations, application systems, allowable costs, and review processes across funder types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Summary / Cover Letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Brief overview of the project, total amount requested, key impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make this concise and compelling — it is often the first (and sometimes only) section a reviewer reads closely. Include 'hook' about impact and the exact funding request. Align language with funder priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Need / Problem Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: What problem will the grant fix? Evidence-based documentation of the need. Local data + national context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use current, localized data anchored in broader national context. Show severity, scope, and why the problem matters to this funder. Avoid generic statements that could apply to any organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goals and Objectives (SMART)
rubrics_metrics.description: Goals: Broad statements of intent. Objectives: Specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, time-bound (SMART).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate broad goals into SMART objectives with clear metrics and timelines. Objectives should map directly to evaluation measures and budgeted activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods / Project Design
rubrics_metrics.description: How will you accomplish the objectives? Who will do the work. Timeline and activities. Population to be served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear, realistic workplan describing activities, responsible staff/partners, schedule, and target population. Ensure methods logically lead to objectives and outcomes; include recruitment/retention strategies if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: How will you measure success? Process evaluation (was the work done?). Outcome evaluation (did it make a difference?). Independent vs. internal evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define indicators, data sources, collection frequency, and responsibility. Distinguish between process metrics and outcome measures; explain whether evaluation will be internal or independent and why. Tie evaluation to objectives and budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Budget Narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel, travel, equipment, indirect costs. Justification for each line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the budget aligns with the narrative and activities. Provide clear line-item justifications and show reasonableness of costs. Follow funder rules on indirect costs and allowable expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: How will the project continue after grant funds end? Other funding sources, built-in revenue, institutional commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe concrete plans for continuation (diverse funding, earned revenue, institutional support). Funders look for realistic exit or continuation strategies; missing sustainability plans are common red flags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Why your organization is best positioned. History of accomplishments. Key staff. Partnerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate relevant track record, staff qualifications, and partner roles. Include examples of past successes and infrastructure (financial systems, program management) that support project delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storytelling approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a storytelling approach with supporting statistics in such a compelling way that the reader can't put down your application until making a positive funding decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blend narrative (beneficiary stories, clear problem-to-solution arc) with evidence. Use anecdotes sparingly and ethically to humanize data; avoid melodrama and unsupported claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Write in short, hard-hitting sentences. Long-winded sentences almost always lose the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer clarity and brevity. Use active voice and single-idea sentences where possible. Edit aggressively to remove filler and jargon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional but engaging. Confident but not arrogant. Specific not vague. Action-oriented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match tone to the funder and context — convey competence and urgency without overclaiming. Avoid passive, vague language that obscures impact or responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common mistakes / anti-patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic language that could fit any organization. Vague objectives without metrics. Budget that doesn't match narrative. Missing sustainability plan. Not following funder guidelines. Submitting late.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this list as a checklist of errors to avoid. Ensure specificity, measurable objectives, narrative-budget alignment, adherence to funder instructions, and on-time submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-proposal research and prospect identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Researching potential funders and identifying prospects before preparing a proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct careful prospect research to match project goals to funder priorities, grant sizes, geographic scope, and application cycles. Use regional associations and databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Inquiry (LOI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparing and submitting LOIs as initial contact with funders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LOIs should be concise, clearly state the ask and fit, and capture the funder's interest. Follow each funder's LOI format and guidance; tailor rather than reuse generic language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online research and systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Using online resources and funder portals (e.g., Grants.gov) to find and apply for grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn funder-specific application systems and deadlines. Maintain up-to-date registrations (e.g., SAM.gov for U.S. federal grants) and templates to streamline submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal grant systems (Grants.gov) familiarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding and navigating federal application systems and requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of federal-specific forms, compliance requirements, and submission processes. Start registration early and follow technical submission instructions precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundation grant systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding private and community foundation processes and expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foundations vary widely in processes and priorities — tailor proposals, follow guidelines, and cultivate relationships. Use foundation-specific forms and respect funding cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logic models and theory of change
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing logic models and articulating the project's theory of change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map inputs → activities → outputs → short/intermediate/long-term outcomes. Clearly state assumptions and causal pathways; tie the logic model to evaluation metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of demographics and statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Employing demographics and statistical evidence to document need and justify approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite reputable, recent sources and use local data where possible. Present statistics visually or succinctly and explain relevance to the target population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation methods (expanded)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selecting appropriate evaluation methods to measure outcomes and processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose qualitative and/or quantitative methods suited to the objectives; specify instruments, sampling, analysis plans, and who will conduct evaluation (internal vs. external). Budget for evaluation activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget development (expanded)
rubrics_metrics.description: Designing a realistic and justified budget that aligns with project activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate costs conservatively, provide clear justification for each line, allocate adequate indirect and administrative costs per funder rules, and ensure budget narratives explain how numbers were derived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site visits and relationship-building
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparing for funder site visits and building relationships with funders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate site visit questions, prepare staff and partners, and use site visits as an opportunity to demonstrate organizational capacity and program fidelity. Cultivate relationships before and after submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Approaches for revising and resubmitting proposals after rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use funder feedback to address weaknesses, strengthen evidence and evaluation, adjust budget alignment, and clarify objectives. Track reviewer comments and demonstrate responsiveness in revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary resources and checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of proposal checklists, glossaries, sample forms, and lists of funders as supporting tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ appendices and checklists to ensure completeness; consult sample grant forms and regional foundation lists to streamline preparation and meet formatting requirements.
